method: Read source and test harness; reread all recorded input hashes and test result. No um.py import, main, Lean rebuild or re-execution of test harness.
findings: Compiler-qualified identity is preserved. Generated declarations need no lexical source match; membership comes from the defining-module metadata and is linked to the source byte hash.
The axiom parser preserves the quoted Unicode names omitted by the former parser; conflicts are explicit errors, missing compiler names/reports are rejected by the caller and index.
Exact qualified names have priority. Ambiguous suffix aliases return a candidate list and no selected source, and aliases do not duplicate proof flags.
The actual receipt records 26797 compiler names, 8317 names with flags, three explicitly absent debt declarations, zero provenance errors and zero proof/flag violations.
Source hash mismatch prevents audited status. The index consumes existing booleans and does not change any flag or gate.
scope_limits: This is an evidence-consuming index, not an independent compiler. Authenticity of declaration metadata, source-hash mapping and audit exit status remains a responsibility of the caller and pinned receipts.
Suffix splitting on a dot inside a quoted identifier may create an unhelpful display alias; exact qualified lookup remains correct and no proof is granted by an alias.
The recorded 14 checks were inspected, not rerun in this independent semantic review.
